target_statement:
theorem actual_potential_geometry {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 2 ≤ κ)
    (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) :
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ :=
    (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) *
      Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)) *
      (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ).transpose
  let f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ := fun x =>
    (WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x) / 2
  ContDiff ℝ ∞ f ∧
    (∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d),
      HasFDerivAt (gradient f) (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin d) A) x) ∧
    StrongConvexOn (Set.univ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) 1 f ∧
    (∀ x y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d),
      ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ κ * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    f 0 = 0 ∧
    (∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), IsMinOn f Set.univ x ↔ x = 0)

actual_consumer_seal.signature:
private theorem actual_first_order_oracle_measurable {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 2 ≤ κ)
    (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) :
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ :=
    (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) *
      Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)) *
      (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ).transpose
  let f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ := fun x =>
    (WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x) / 2
  let query : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) :=
    fun x => WithLp.toLp 2 (A *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)
  @Measurable (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (borel (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)))
    (borel (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)))
    (fun x => (f x, query x))

open_internal_obligations.statement: Index and arithmetic expansion: 1<=i<=d and d>=2 imply 0<(i-1/2)pi/d<pi
Diagonal Lambda is symmetric, so (O Lambda O^T)^T=O Lambda O^T
Square real O^T O=I implies O O^T=I and ||O^T x||=||x||
x^T A x=sum_i lambda_i ((O^T x)_i)^2; eigenvalue bounds imply ||O^T x||^2 <= x^T A x <= kappa||O^T x||^2. This node does not yet replace ||O^T x|| by ||x||.
The source introduction says the hard family belongs to the prescribed class: combine symmetry with Loewner bounds
A fixed finite real quadratic polynomial is C^infinity; no positivity or invertibility is required for regularity
For symmetric A: Df_A(x)[h]=<Ax,h>; grad f_A(x)=Ax; D^2f_A(x)[h,k]=<Ah,k>, Hessian matrix A
On all Euclidean R^d, Hessian lower bound I gives strong convexity with coefficient 1/2 in the first-order inequality; symmetric Hessian bounds 0<=H<=kappa I give kappa-Lipschitz gradient
For each fixed A, the literal numeric pair x |-> (x^T A x/2,Ax) is continuous into R x R^d. No differentiability or actual-gradient identification is required for this numeric-map branch.

For each fixed hard-family input, the actual value-and-Euclidean-gradient oracle is Borel. Both numeric-pair continuity and the separately discharged actual-gradient identification are required; no joint/adaptive measurability theorem is asserted.

Prove internally for every x that gradient f_A(x)=Ax (in the exact Euclidean carrier, query x=toLp 2 (A *v ofLp x)); hence (f_A(x),query x) is the actual value-and-gradient oracle, not merely a named numeric pair.
